headline: High: Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing can ingest Caveman-authored content and act on it, creating prompt-injection and data-leak paths; Caveman’s MCP use raises interaction risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Caveman can use MCP and writes project files like CLAUDE.md, while Perplexity runs vendor-hosted browsing/search and can ingest uploaded or web content. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if Caveman output is copied into Perplexity or vice versa. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so I rate this above low.
conditions: IF Caveman output is pasted into Perplexity prompts or uploads
IF Perplexity browsing results are copied into Caveman-managed instruction files
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of model-generated text into instruction files
Add a provenance prefix to all imported snippets
Review any Perplexity-sourced text before placing it in CLAUDE.md
Use separate workspaces for instructions and research
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Perplexity uploads documents and sends queries to vendor APIs. If the same sensitive material is shared between them, Perplexity can transmit it off-host. Caveman has no network egress, but that does not block leakage once data reaches Perplexity.
conditions: IF sensitive project notes or memory files are copied into Perplexity uploads
IF Perplexity is used on documents containing secrets or private logs
mitigations: Redact secrets before uploading documents
Keep session logs out of Perplexity inputs
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for research
Turn off sharing of generated summaries outside the team
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP, while Perplexity supports multiple instances with shared state across sessions for the same user. However, Perplexity cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, and Caveman’s profile does not show shared write access to the same mutable resources. The overlap is mostly read/coordination, so conflict risk is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through MCP or a shared service
IF Caveman is configured to write to a shared git or filesystem target
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Lock shared resources before running either agent
Use read-only access for Perplexity research
requires-engineering: add resource locking around shared targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is a search-RAG answer engine with live web search and citations, and Caveman is a content-writing agent that can consume files and project notes. If Caveman output is treated as authoritative research input, Perplexity can amplify an error into polished but wrong downstream content. The pair lacks a built-in verification loop, so the cascade is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF Caveman-generated notes are used as source material for Perplexity answers
IF Perplexity outputs are reused by Caveman without human verification
mitigations: Require human review before reuse of outputs
Cross-check claims against primary sources
Mark generated text as untrusted until verified
Separate drafting from fact-finding steps
requires-engineering: add automated citation verification

E_compliance.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while Perplexity processes uploaded documents and browsing context under vendor-hosted service terms. If regulated or sensitive data is moved from Caveman-managed notes into Perplexity uploads, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data from Caveman notes is uploaded into Perplexity
IF the organization requires local-only retention for session logs or project notes
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Perplexity inputs
Review vendor privacy terms before use
Keep a local-only copy of sensitive notes
Document retention expectations for both tools
requires-engineering: route regulated data to a compliant system
